items.headline: US proposes new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, with apparel hubs Vietnam, Bangladesh and Cambodia named
items.summary: USTR Jamieson Greer found that 'structural excess capacity' practices in 14 economies are actionable under Section 301 and proposed extra tariffs: up to 35% on Vietnam (20% with a deal), up to 25% on India (17% with a deal), up to 20% on China and Singapore, up to 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, and 15% caps for the EU, Japan, Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan. USTR singles out ready-made garments for Bangladesh, apparel for Cambodia, textiles and apparel for Indonesia, and textiles, apparel and footwear for Vietnam. Nothing takes effect yet: comments are due 5 January 2027 and hearings start 25 January 2027, and Flexport notes final rates could differ.
items.why_it_matters: Sourcing-cost pressure on brands buying from Asia squeezes content budgets too; cheaper, faster product imagery becomes an easier sell in 2027 planning.
items.note: Also covered by CNBC and Sourcing Journal (not readable this run). Image link is USTR's share graphic, not downloaded (workspace network blocked).

items.headline: Shein's Q3 profit rises as cost cuts offset a 28% drop in European revenue
items.summary: Shein's net revenue fell 5.9% to $10.3 billion in the quarter to September, but adjusted net profit rose about 27% to $790 million and adjusted EBIT 45.6% to $948 million as operating costs fell 7.1%. Europe revenue dropped 27.6% to EUR2.98 billion after the EU removed the EUR150 duty exemption and added a EUR3 duty per item category; US revenue fell 9.4% to $2.37 billion, while active customers grew to 291 million from 265 million. Management expects Europe to stay under pressure from the EU's new EUR2 handling fee (from 1 November) and is shifting to local fulfilment, which covered over 40% of European deliveries. Reported net profit of $4.65 billion includes a large non-cash fair-value gain.
items.why_it_matters: Ultra-fast fashion is now margin-led, not volume-led; leaner catalogue operations and cheaper per-SKU imagery are part of that playbook.
items.note: FashionNetwork also covered it (not readable this run). Investing.com lead image is a Reuters photo; not stored.

items.headline: Veruschka, the 1960s supermodel of 'Blow-Up' and 13 American Vogue covers, dies at 87
items.summary: German model Vera von Lehndorff, known as Veruschka, died at home in Berlin on 24 November, her sister confirmed. Discovered in Florence in 1959, she became one of the best-paid models of her era, shot by Richard Avedon and Irving Penn, appeared on 13 American Vogue covers and played herself in Antonioni's 1966 film 'Blow-Up'. From the mid-1970s she worked on body-painting photography with artist Holger Truelzsch, and returned to the runway for Giles Deacon in 2011. Ground News counts more than 100 outlets covering her death; photographer Nigel Barker and former partner Franco Rubartelli posted tributes.
items.note: Sources: Parade and Hello! via Yahoo; Ground News aggregation. WWD obituary not readable this run. No photos stored (real person).

items.headline: Adobe: AI-referred visits to US retail sites are up 127% this season, ahead of a $6.9B Thanksgiving
items.summary: US shoppers spent more than $82.5 billion online from 1 to 22 November, up 9.1% year on year, according to Adobe Analytics, with two days already above $4 billion. Visits referred by AI tools to US retailer sites are up 127%, and Adobe expects jumps of 159% on Thanksgiving and 95% on Black Friday; it forecasts $47.5 billion for the Cyber 5 period, with Black Friday at $12.9 billion and Thanksgiving at $6.9 billion. Salesforce separately expects $75.8 billion of $357 billion in global Cyber Week sales to be influenced by AI tools, including agents.
items.why_it_matters: AI assistants are now a real traffic source; brands need product images and data that read well to agents and convert when the shopper lands.
items.note: No apparel-specific figures given. Lead image not checked; not stored.

items.headline: Bangladesh sets a 36% higher garment minimum wage; unions say it falls short
items.summary: Bangladesh's garment wage board agreed on 25 November to raise the minimum monthly wage from 12,500 to 17,000 taka (about $137), a 36% rise, with higher grades up to 21,500 taka; it applies from December, with new pay from January (FashionUnited; Al Jazeera, which cites 17,500 taka). Workers had demanded 30,000-32,000 taka, and the Clean Clothes Campaign called the rise insufficient and urged brands to raise purchase prices. The labour representative on the board urged workers back to factories after weeks of protests that the BGMEA says cost an estimated $428 million.
items.note: Update to the 24 and 25 Nov items: the wage is now set. Sources differ on the headline figure (17,000 vs 17,500 taka) and on the demand (30,000 vs 32,000). News photos show workers; not stored.

items.headline: Callimacus launches 'Magic', a self-serve AI site builder that rebuilds a fashion brand's website from its URL
items.summary: Callimacus has released Magic, a self-serve version of its composable website framework for fashion brands (The Interline). A brand enters its current web address and gets a new 'pageless' preview within hours, which it can adapt with natural-language prompts; the trial is free and paid plans publish to the brand's own domain or a subdomain. It connects to Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Shopify and WordPress, and The Interline links the concept to Solomei AI, the Brunello Cucinelli spin-out.
items.why_it_matters: Prompt-built storefronts will need a steady feed of on-brand imagery; a potential integration or co-marketing partner for On-Model.
items.note: Image is a supplied UI screenshot (credit: Callimacus); link kept, not downloaded (workspace network blocked).

items.headline: IFM's FashionReboot: L'Oreal chases AI-answer citations and LVMH tracks its AI footprint
items.summary: FashionUnited's recap of four AI sessions at the Institut Francais de la Mode's FashionReboot 2026 conference: L'Oreal's global head of search said the group (40 brands, 700 websites) now optimises to be cited in AI answers and is testing in-AI purchasing with Google and OpenAI in the US. LVMH's VP of AI transformation said the group measures its AI footprint internally, and better forecasting let one beauty brand move shipments from air to sea. A final panel on image production raised copyright and image homogenisation concerns.
items.why_it_matters: Big luxury and beauty groups are worried about AI imagery looking generic; brand-consistent, controllable output is the counter-argument.
items.note: Published 24 Nov 06:00 UTC, just before this window; not in earlier digests. Conference photos; not stored.

items.headline: The Interline: measure Black Friday by incremental demand, not the sales spike
items.summary: In an Interline opinion piece, Pattern's Luke Elliott argues headline Black Friday sales don't show whether promotions created demand or just pulled it forward. He suggests October as a baseline, measuring through mid-January, comparing Amazon with the brand's own site, finding the minimum effective discount per SKU and tracking whether promo buyers come back at full price. He also flags the EU's lowest-30-day-price rule as a timing constraint.
items.note: Opinion piece. Lead image not checked; not stored.
